_comment: Manual corrections applied by scripts/build_policy.py --overrides on top of the model's structure. Written by the Claude session that built Stage 3, NOT by a human reviewer -- each is a judgment to check against policy/expense_policy.md. Every entry is copied into policy_v1.json's build_meta.manual_edits with its reason and the value it replaced.

10.4._reason: The model turned 'pre-approval required above 15,000 / $200' into a hard per-event limit as well as an approval threshold. Exceeding a threshold that needs approval must read as needs_approval, not violation. Also removed an unconditional 'preapproval_evidence' documentation item: approval is already checked through requires_approval_above, and the item would make every event under the threshold 'unknown'.

11.2._reason: Same defect as 10.4: 'more than 5,000 requires approval' is an approval threshold, not a cap.

15.1._reason: Same defect as 10.4: the 50,000 figure is the level above which an L5+ approver is needed, not a cap on training spend.

15.3._reason: The model made 50,000 a hard limit. The clause says a course above 50,000 needs a signed service bond: a requirement that applies only above the threshold, i.e. 'not above 50,000 OR bond signed'.

conditions.text: the course costs no more than 50,000, or the employee has signed the 12-month service retention bond

any_of.text: the amount is no more than 50,000
a 12-month service retention bond was signed before enrolment

20.1._reason: The model structured the receipt thresholds (500 / $10) as per-claim LIMITS and as failing conditions, so any expense of 500 or more would read as a violation. They are thresholds for a documentation requirement, per currency.

20.2._reason: The model used the 'amount' quantity for a cumulative monthly figure (it would compare one bill to 3,000 twice). Kept as the monthly aggregate limit; the 'below the receipt threshold' condition is the numeric amount < 500. NOTE: the clause means all self-declared expenses across categories, but monthly aggregation here is per category.

conditions.text: the expense is below the 500 receipt threshold (self-declaration is only for these)

21.1._reason: A submission deadline is a time window, not a per-day amount limit: requires days_since_expense <= 30.

conditions.text: the expense is submitted within 30 days of the expense date

21.2._reason: A window measured from the employee's return from a trip: trip dates are not extracted, so this is a judgment that will usually be unknown, not a per-day limit.

conditions.text: the expense is submitted within 60 days of the employee's return from the international trip

21.3._reason: 'Ordinarily one claim per trip' is guidance, not something checkable on one expense; the model invented a count limit of 1 that is not in the text.

21.4._reason: The model used the 'days' quantity (trip days) for 'older than 90 days from the expense date' and left a per-day unit; it must be days_since_expense > 90.

conditions.text: the claim is more than 90 days after the expense date

23.1._reason: Approval routing by claim TOTAL (section 23) cannot be checked on one expense; it is Stage 6's approval workflow. The model turned the tiers into per-claim limits.

23.2._reason: Approval routing by claim total: informational for Stage 3 (see 23.1).

23.3._reason: Approval routing by claim total: informational for Stage 3 (see 23.1).

23.4._reason: Approval routing by claim total: informational for Stage 3 (see 23.1).

23.5._reason: The policy-exception rule (a breach needs written justification and one level more approval) is a consequence of a violation, applied by the approval workflow (Stage 6), not a check on one expense.

24.1._reason: Never structured by the model (its daily quota ran out before section 24). Duplicate-claim detection is Stage 4 (fraud) and cannot be judged from one expense.
24.1.notes: Informational here: duplicate detection is Stage 4.

24.2._reason: Never structured by the model (quota). Claim-splitting detection needs cross-claim analysis: Stage 4.
24.2.notes: Informational here: claim splitting is Stage 4.

24.3._reason: Never structured by the model (quota). Tamper detection is Stage 4.
24.3.notes: Informational here: tamper detection is Stage 4.

24.4._reason: Never structured by the model (quota). Double-reimbursement detection needs data Stage 1 does not extract: Stage 4.
24.4.notes: Informational here: double reimbursement is Stage 4.

24.5._reason: Statement about audits and consequences; not checkable on an expense.

8.6._reason: The 7,500 threshold was structured both as the documentation threshold AND as a 'requires amount >= 7,500' condition, so a Rs 5,000 hotel bill would fail the condition. It is only a threshold for the GST-invoice requirement (documentation min_amount).

5.3._reason: The model added an unconditional 'receipt' documentation requirement that 5.3 does not state (receipt rules are 5.4 / 20.1); it would make every ride unknown.

3.2._reason: The model compared the 'days' quantity (trip days) with 7 and 14 as if it were booking lead time. Booking date vs travel date is not extracted, so this is a judgment that will usually be unknown.

conditions.text: domestic tickets were booked at least 7 days ahead and international tickets at least 14 days ahead, or a documented urgent business reason exists

4.2._reason: 'Rail or bus should be preferred ... under 400 km' is guidance ('should'), not a prohibition; the model made air travel under 400 km an excluded circumstance using a route distance that is not extracted.

12.2._reason: Home broadband is reimbursable for 'L4 and above OR any role designated remote/field-based': the model AND-ed the two conditions and restricted the limit entry to grades L4-L6, so a designated remote L2 would find no limit. Now one any_of condition and an unrestricted 1,500 limit.

conditions.text: the employee is grade L4 or above, or the role is formally designated remote/field-based by HR

any_of.text: the role is designated remote or field-based by HR

12.3._reason: 'Reimbursable only with pre-approval, capped at 3,000 per trip (or actuals with WRITTEN pre-approval for a higher amount)': above 3,000 is allowed with written approval, so it is an approval matter, not a violation. Structured as approval always required; the 3,000 figure is kept in notes. Unconditional 'bill'/'preapproval_email' documentation items removed (the approval requirement covers the latter).
12.3.notes: Cap is 3,000 per trip; above that, WRITTEN pre-approval is required. This structure only records that approval is always required.

12.4._reason: Removed an unconditional 'bill' documentation item (the document IS the bill); the substantive rule is the billed-to-name condition.

9.1._reason: Receipts are required only when the employee chooses actuals over the per diem; the model made 'receipt' unconditional, which would make every travel-meal unit unknown. Documentation removed; the per-trip method choice stays a judgment condition.

16.1._reason: The model added an unconditional 'receipt' documentation item the clause does not state (receipts are governed by 20.1); it would make every unit unknown.
